topic: AI Capstone Planning and System Design
learningObjectives: Define the problem and requirements for an AI project
Select suitable data, models, and system components
Design a complete architecture for an AI capstone

activities.title: Problem-to-Solution Map
activities.instruction: Explore how a real-world problem connects to AI solution components.

content.concept: A strong AI project begins by connecting a clearly defined problem to measurable requirements and suitable technical components.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Clearly defines the real-world problem the project aims to address.
Identifies the people or systems that will use or be affected by the solution.
Describes the functional and technical needs of the project.
Identifies the information required to develop and operate the AI system.
Defines the ML, deep learning, or generative AI technique suited to the problem.
Describes the application, API, model, storage, and other technical parts.
Defines measurable criteria used to evaluate whether the solution works.

activities.title: Choose the AI Approach
activities.instruction: Select an appropriate AI approach for each project requirement.

content.concept: The problem type, available data, expected output, and constraints influence the choice of ML or generative AI approach.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Capstone Architecture
activities.instruction: Build the end-to-end architecture for an AI application.

content.concept: An AI capstone can connect users, applications, APIs, data pipelines, models, storage, and monitoring into one system.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Project Execution Roadmap
activities.instruction: Arrange the major milestones for completing the capstone.

content.concept: A practical AI project progresses through requirements, data preparation, development, evaluation, deployment, and demonstration.
